{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Port the five modules as native Spring Cloud Stream-style processor modules in the s-c-s repository, preserving externally visible XD configuration properties and message semantics where practical.",
    "Use the repository's existing build system, Java version, dependency-management conventions, module layout, and test framework rather than introducing new infrastructure.",
    "Implement json-to-tuple and object-to-json using the existing JSON and message-conversion facilities available in the target repository, with explicit handling for malformed input based on existing project conventions.",
    "Implement script using the supported scripting engine and expose script configuration through the module's processor properties; avoid adding a new scripting language unless required by the existing XD behavior.",
    "Implement shell with controlled process execution, configurable command and arguments, stream handling, exit-code/error behavior, and resource cleanup.",
    "Implement splitter as a message-producing processor that supports the expected delimiter or collection-based splitting behavior and preserves relevant message headers.",
    "Treat composed-job removal and composed-job persistence as design investigations/spikes because the stories explicitly request exploration rather than a production implementation.",
    "For composed-job persistence, evaluate ZooKeeper metadata as the authoritative serialized definition store and document versioning, atomicity, recovery, compatibility, and cleanup considerations.",
    "Introduce BinderFactory as a small abstraction with a default implementation for the currently supported binder and an extension point for additional binder types.",
    "Add unit and integration coverage for each ported module and for BinderFactory behavior, using mocks for external systems and subprocesses where practical."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The XD source implementations, documentation, examples, and relevant tests are available locally or in accessible repositories.",
    "The target s-c-s repository already builds successfully and provides standard module templates, messaging APIs, configuration conventions, and test infrastructure.",
    "The increment targets the existing supported Java and Spring versions of s-c-s; no framework-wide upgrade or migration is required.",
    "The five module ports are functional ports rather than exact byte-for-byte reproductions of all historical XD internals.",
    "Existing module conventions are sufficient for packaging, registration, configuration metadata, and local execution; no new deployment platform integration is required.",
    "The script module only needs to support the scripting engine and language combinations already supported or readily available in the target project.",
    "The shell module does not require operating-system-specific command emulation; tests will use portable commands or test doubles.",
    "The composed-job stories require an options analysis, recommendation, and technical design, but not implementation, migration, or production rollout in this increment.",
    "ZooKeeper integration for the composed-job investigation can be assessed using existing repository abstractions and does not require deploying a new production ZooKeeper cluster.",
    "Backward compatibility testing is limited to documented behavior and representative examples; exhaustive compatibility testing against all historical XD versions is out of scope.",
    "Effort includes development, code review preparation, automated tests, documentation, and local verification performed by one developer, but excludes elapsed waiting time and external stakeholder approvals."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Repository and source discovery",
      "activity_description": "Inspect the s-c-s repository structure, build conventions, existing processor modules, binder usage, test patterns, and the corresponding XD implementations. Produce a porting map and identify API or behavior differences.",
      "most_likely_effort": 16
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Module scaffolding and build integration",
      "activity_description": "Create or adapt the common module structure, dependencies, configuration metadata, registration, packaging, and local build wiring needed by the five processor modules.",
      "most_likely_effort": 12
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Port json-to-tuple processor",
      "activity_description": "Implement the json-to-tuple processor, port configuration and conversion behavior, handle invalid input according to project conventions, and add focused unit tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 20
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Port object-to-json processor",
      "activity_description": "Implement the object-to-json processor, preserve supported serialization options and message behavior, and add focused unit tests for representative object and error cases.",
      "most_likely_effort": 20
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Port script processor",
      "activity_description": "Implement script evaluation and message exchange, expose required script and execution properties, manage execution errors and returned values, and add unit tests using representative scripts.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Port shell processor",
      "activity_description": "Implement external command invocation, input and output handling, configurable arguments and environment behavior, exit-code/error processing, timeout or cleanup safeguards, and tests using controlled commands or mocks.",
      "most_likely_effort": 28
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Port splitter processor",
      "activity_description": "Implement splitting of supported payload types, configure delimiter or splitting behavior as required by the XD contract, preserve applicable headers, and add unit tests for normal and edge cases.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Cross-module integration, documentation, and packaging validation",
      "activity_description": "Run the complete build and representative streaming-pipeline tests, resolve inter-module integration issues, verify configuration metadata and artifacts, add usage documentation and examples, and perform regression cleanup.",
      "most_likely_effort": 36
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "Composed-job removal options investigation",
      "activity_description": "Trace composed-job lifecycle, resource ownership, cleanup paths, and current consumers; evaluate alternatives for removing composed jobs; document risks, compatibility impacts, recommended approach, and follow-up implementation work.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Composed-job ZooKeeper persistence options investigation",
      "activity_description": "Assess schemas and serialization formats for storing composed-job definitions in ZooKeeper metadata, recovery and recreation flows, versioning, atomic writes, failure handling, cleanup, and security implications; produce a recommendation and design notes.",
      "most_likely_effort": 28
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A11",
      "activity_name": "BinderFactory abstraction",
      "activity_description": "Define the BinderFactory interface and lifecycle contract, implement the current binder-backed default, adapt existing callers, provide extension points for future binder types, and add unit tests for selection and failure behavior.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A12",
      "activity_name": "Final verification and delivery preparation",
      "activity_description": "Perform final clean-build verification, execute the relevant automated test suite, review changed APIs and documentation, check licensing and dependency impact, and prepare the increment for submission.",
      "most_likely_effort": 20
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 292
  }
}
message.reasoning:
**Assessing project assumptions**

I’m thinking about the source and compatibility baseline for this project, but there seems to be a lack of acceptance from stakeholders. It’s possibly about Spring XD and whether it relates to an unknown aspect of s-c-s. I want to create a map of activities across the board. Also, I think it’s important to keep technical decisions clear and concise, perhaps using JSON arrays to organize everything effectively.

technical_and_design_decisions: Port the five modules as native Spring Cloud Stream-style processor modules in the s-c-s repository, preserving externally visible XD configuration properties and message semantics where practical.
Use the repository's existing build system, Java version, dependency-management conventions, module layout, and test framework rather than introducing new infrastructure.

Implement json-to-tuple and object-to-json using the existing JSON and message-conversion facilities available in the target repository, with explicit handling for malformed input based on existing project conventions.

Implement script using the supported scripting engine and expose script configuration through the module's processor properties; avoid adding a new scripting language unless required by the existing XD behavior.
Implement shell with controlled process execution, configurable command and arguments, stream handling, exit-code/error behavior, and resource cleanup.
Implement splitter as a message-producing processor that supports the expected delimiter or collection-based splitting behavior and preserves relevant message headers.
Treat composed-job removal and composed-job persistence as design investigations/spikes because the stories explicitly request exploration rather than a production implementation.
For composed-job persistence, evaluate ZooKeeper metadata as the authoritative serialized definition store and document versioning, atomicity, recovery, compatibility, and cleanup considerations.
Introduce BinderFactory as a small abstraction with a default implementation for the currently supported binder and an extension point for additional binder types.
Add unit and integration coverage for each ported module and for BinderFactory behavior, using mocks for external systems and subprocesses where practical.
assumptions: The XD source implementations, documentation, examples, and relevant tests are available locally or in accessible repositories.
The target s-c-s repository already builds successfully and provides standard module templates, messaging APIs, configuration conventions, and test infrastructure.
The increment targets the existing supported Java and Spring versions of s-c-s; no framework-wide upgrade or migration is required.
The five module ports are functional ports rather than exact byte-for-byte reproductions of all historical XD internals.
Existing module conventions are sufficient for packaging, registration, configuration metadata, and local execution; no new deployment platform integration is required.
The script module only needs to support the scripting engine and language combinations already supported or readily available in the target project.
The shell module does not require operating-system-specific command emulation; tests will use portable commands or test doubles.
The composed-job stories require an options analysis, recommendation, and technical design, but not implementation, migration, or production rollout in this increment.
ZooKeeper integration for the composed-job investigation can be assessed using existing repository abstractions and does not require deploying a new production ZooKeeper cluster.
Backward compatibility testing is limited to documented behavior and representative examples; exhaustive compatibility testing against all historical XD versions is out of scope.

Effort includes development, code review preparation, automated tests, documentation, and local verification performed by one developer, but excludes elapsed waiting time and external stakeholder approvals.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the s-c-s repository structure, build conventions, existing processor modules, binder usage, test patterns, and the corresponding XD implementations. Produce a porting map and identify API or behavior differences.
Create or adapt the common module structure, dependencies, configuration metadata, registration, packaging, and local build wiring needed by the five processor modules.
Implement the json-to-tuple processor, port configuration and conversion behavior, handle invalid input according to project conventions, and add focused unit tests.
Implement the object-to-json processor, preserve supported serialization options and message behavior, and add focused unit tests for representative object and error cases.
Implement script evaluation and message exchange, expose required script and execution properties, manage execution errors and returned values, and add unit tests using representative scripts.

Implement external command invocation, input and output handling, configurable arguments and environment behavior, exit-code/error processing, timeout or cleanup safeguards, and tests using controlled commands or mocks.
Implement splitting of supported payload types, configure delimiter or splitting behavior as required by the XD contract, preserve applicable headers, and add unit tests for normal and edge cases.

activities.activity_name: Cross-module integration, documentation, and packaging validation
activities.activity_description: Run the complete build and representative streaming-pipeline tests, resolve inter-module integration issues, verify configuration metadata and artifacts, add usage documentation and examples, and perform regression cleanup.

Trace composed-job lifecycle, resource ownership, cleanup paths, and current consumers; evaluate alternatives for removing composed jobs; document risks, compatibility impacts, recommended approach, and follow-up implementation work.

Assess schemas and serialization formats for storing composed-job definitions in ZooKeeper metadata, recovery and recreation flows, versioning, atomic writes, failure handling, cleanup, and security implications; produce a recommendation and design notes.

Define the BinderFactory interface and lifecycle contract, implement the current binder-backed default, adapt existing callers, provide extension points for future binder types, and add unit tests for selection and failure behavior.

Perform final clean-build verification, execute the relevant automated test suite, review changed APIs and documentation, check licensing and dependency impact, and prepare the increment for submission.
